title: MySQL logs
context: What are the main MySQL logs, and what does each do?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): MySQL questions
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: The redo log records page changes so InnoDB can replay committed work after a crash. The undo log stores old row versions, so transactions can roll back and readers can see consistent snapshots. The binary log (binlog) records every committed change at the logical level and is used for replication and point-in-time restore. The slow query log records slow statements, and the error log records server problems. Redo and undo are InnoDB internals. The binlog is what replicas read.

points.title: Redo for crash recovery
points.why: Redo lets InnoDB recover committed changes after a crash.

points.title: Binlog for replication
points.why: Replicas apply the binary log, so it must be enabled for replication and point-in-time recovery.

points.title: Undo for rollback
points.why: Undo supports rollback and consistent reads.
